data.description:
## Description

**What**: New GitHub Actions workflow file (separate from .github/workflows/ci.yml) that triggers on push to `story/**` branch pattern. Workflow fetches the session branch, computes diff scope as `merge-base(session, story/<branch>)..story/<branch>`, dispatches ci-llm-review-runner.sh on that scope, and writes findings via GitHubPRDefenseStore.load_for_region. Concurrency-group keyed `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID }}` (vars context — env not allowed in concurrency expressions per GitHub Actions docs).
**Why**: Walking-skeleton CI per-story review.

**Scope**:
- IN: New workflow file (.github/workflows/sprint-story-review.yml or similar)
- IN: Push trigger on story/** pattern
- IN: Session-branch fetch + merge-base diff computation
- IN: Concurrency-group expression using vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID
- IN: GitHubPRDefenseStore.load_for_region activation in CI llm-review path
- OUT: Strategy E region-split — owned by S9
- OUT: Hash-of-record protocol — owned by S10

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, a push to story/<id> triggers the new workflow and runs ci-llm-review-runner.sh against `merge-base(session, story/<id>)..story/<id>`
  ← Satisfies: "SC5: CI llm-review fires on push to story/* branches scoped to merge-base"
- When this story is complete, the concurrency-group expression `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID }}` parses without error in a test workflow
  ← Satisfies: "SC5: vars context (not env)"
- When this story is complete, a second push to the same story/<id> triggers a CI run that reads prior attestations from GitHubPRDefenseStore (asserted via fixture)
  ← Satisfies: "SC5: PR-scoped GitHubPRDefenseStore active from day one"
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Reliability] Pick a vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID materialization mechanism: (a) committed file in session branch; (b) GitHub repo variable set by Phase A via gh api; (c) workflow input derived from branch name pattern. Each option has distinct security and concurrency implications: a committed file leaks session ID across forks; a repo variable requires write permission; a branch-name-derived ID couples concurrency keying to naming convention. Document the choice and add a test asserting concurrency-group expression resolves correctly under parallel pushes.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a CI runner, llm-review fires on every push to story/* branches scoped to the per-story delta, with concurrency-group preventing rate-limit storms
